statements.quote: Remember — Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment is Returning! This time, to Los Angeles on May 18th!
statements.context: Closing promotional block of a mentalizing column. The author's event series Rapid Acting Mental Health Treatment (RAMHT) returns to Los Angeles on May 18 (2025) at the Skyline Loft, 224 East 11th Street, during the APA meeting; a 13-name speaker lineup follows (Grady Hannah, Kellie Newsome, Carlene MacMillan, Daniel Karlin, Jay Sanguinetti, Sandhya Prashad, Sarah Norman, Chris Aiken, Oded Kraft, Dominik Middelmann, Jonathan Seltzer, Jonathan Downar, Chris Dougherty).
statements.note: Own-event announcement (RAMHT); coder may mark CONTROL. Compound: date, city, venue and speaker lineup.

statements.quote: We are approaching the “leftover loss threshold.” ... We are closer and closer to the asymptote of unbelievable suffering in our experience.
statements.context: Essay arguing the 'mental health crisis' is a crisis of hopelessness. Using The Leftovers (2% of people vanish = 2000/100,000) as an 'unimaginable loss' benchmark, the author says US death rates and suicidal-ideation rates are moving toward that threshold; a trend claim implying continued worsening.
statements.note: Borderline: present-tense trend claim implying continued approach to a threshold; no date or quantity to resolve. Two adjacent sentences joined.

statements.quote: Keep in mind the best predictor of completing suicide is attempted suicide. Those attempts will turn into completed suicides later. We don’t know which ones.
statements.context: After CDC youth data (nearly 1 in 3 girls seriously considered suicide, up about 60% in a decade; rising attempt rates), the author states that some of today's suicide attempts will become completed suicides in the future.
statements.note: Population-level expectation; direction only, no quantity or date.

statements.quote: And it's only going in the wrong direction:
statements.context: Caption to an embedded interactive map of US gun violence (Gun Violence Archive), after noting the 2022 Parkland-survivor protests and a June 23 ruling expanding gun access; the author says gun violence keeps trending worse.
statements.note: Borderline trend claim about gun violence; no date or quantity.

statements.quote: It is not stopping. Our hearts will be ground into the dirt.
statements.context: Footnote 1 to the opening content warning of the essay on suicide, loss and hopelessness; the author asserts the crisis is not stopping and will keep grinding people down.
statements.note: Rhetorical but sincere; open-ended, no date.

statements.quote: If you want to hear what the team at MDhub has to say for themselves, their cofounder is speaking at rapid acting mental health treatment on May 18 in Los Angeles with me!
statements.context: In a post on everyday AI uses, the author says MDHub (the AI scribe he uses in clinic) will have its cofounder speak at the author's RAMHT event on May 18 in Los Angeles. Post 1 of this packet names Dominik Middelmann, Co-Founder and CEO of MDHub, in the lineup.
statements.note: Own-event speaker announcement; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: I'm due for a midlife crisis, I know. But those are not free. Usually there is a foreign car involved. Those are likely to have significant tariffs.
statements.context: Joke post about 'deferring' his 46th birthday because of tariffs and an unsettled economy; the author says a midlife-crisis foreign car is likely to carry significant tariffs.
statements.note: Satirical frame (deferring aging); the tariff claim itself reads as sincere. Low forecast value.

statements.quote: Here is the poster we have accepted to the APA annual meeting.
statements.context: Post on Dr. Irfan Handoo's flexibly dosed weekly IV ketamine protocol (57% remission in an open-label sample). The author says the poster he co-authored (with Handoo and Amna Aslam) is accepted for the APA annual meeting, implying it will be presented there (May 2025).
statements.note: Borderline: acceptance is past, presentation is upcoming; own-work item, coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: Stay tuned for my upcoming podcast episodes with Dr Irfan Handoo!
statements.context: Closing line of the ketamine dosing post; the author promises future podcast episodes with Dr. Irfan Handoo about his weekly flexibly dosed ketamine protocol.
statements.note: Own-newsletter content promise; coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: I have an in-person, live, exciting, and other adjectives, newsletter event in Los Angeles on May 18, with a thrilling speaker line up. We're going to be announcing brand new treatments for depression, for heaven's sake.
statements.context: Promotional aside in the author's intro to a guest article by Alex (physicist) on once-daily lithium dosing. The author's RAMHT event in Los Angeles on May 18 will include announcements of 'brand new treatments for depression'.
statements.note: Own-event announcement; compound (date/city + new-treatment announcements); coder may mark CONTROL.

statements.quote: In this case, there seem to be many sensible reasons why multiple daily dose regimens became common practice and why they are now being replaced by once-daily dosing regimens.
statements.context: Guest article by Alex (physicist and psychiatric patient), hosted by the author, on why lithium moved to multiple daily dosing after the 1970s 'kidney scare'. Alex states that multiple-daily regimens are now being replaced by once-daily dosing. The author's intro endorses the once-daily punchline ('it should probably be dosed just once a day').
statements.note: Guest author's (Alex) present-tense practice-trend claim; author hosts and agrees with once-daily but does not restate the trend. Borderline.

statements.quote: I have never been more correct in my life about anything than when I advocated for shorting the stock of UnitedHealth Group.
statements.context: On the day UnitedHealth Group shares collapsed after CEO Andrew Witty's abrupt resignation (2025-05-14), the author restates his earlier call to short UNH stock (links to his earlier post 'Short Sell United Healthcare (or your big health player of choice)') and claims vindication.
statements.note: Restatement/self-assessment of an earlier short-UNH call, not a new forward call; logged for linkage.

statements.quote: Don’t worry, he still has insider trading investigations by the DOJ to be deposed in the discovery phase, as I satirized here.
statements.context: After describing Witty's resignation and UNH's roughly $300 billion market-cap loss, the author expects Witty to still face deposition in the discovery phase of DOJ insider-trading investigations; links to the author's earlier satire on the topic.
statements.note: Expectation that Witty will be deposed in DOJ insider-trading probes; phrased with a nod to the author's own satire piece.

statements.quote: and then Trump goes and blows up Pharmacy Benefit Managers, maybe, and it was all too much.
statements.context: Listing pressures behind Witty's exit (walked-back earnings guidance, shareholder lawsuits, DOJ cases), the author says Trump is moving against pharmacy benefit managers, hedged with 'maybe', as a factor in UNH's collapse.
statements.note: Borderline: hedged present-tense description of a pending policy action against PBMs; not clearly a forward call.

statements.quote: We wanted corporate responsibility, and we may or may not get it, yet. But the market has spoken, for the time being.
statements.context: Closing of the post; the author credits media pressure (ProPublica, American Prospect, his readers) for the market's reaction to UNH and is uncertain whether corporate accountability will follow the share collapse.
statements.note: Explicitly uncertain ('may or may not'); no direction.

statements.quote: I have decided to step down as Chief Executive officer of our company. I will remain as a senior adviser to our new CEO Steve Hemsley.
statements.context: Quoted internal letter from UNH CEO Andrew Witty, sent to the author by a laid-off former employee and described by the author as unverified; Witty says he will stay on as senior adviser to new CEO Steve Hemsley.
statements.note: Quoted third party (Witty's letter); the author reproduces it without adopting or disputing it.
